blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Covers procedural and legal classifications under Types of Companies.
Details the steps, documentation, and compliance required for Formation and Incorporation.
Focuses on legal provisions governing Company Directors and Management.
Outlines the framework and regulatory methods for the Winding Up of Companies.

cells: Restrict transfer of shares; limit members to 200; cannot invite public subscriptions
Name ends with 'Private Limited'; min 2 and max 200 members
Shares freely transferable; can invite public to subscribe shares/debentures
Name ends with 'Limited'; min 7 members; min 3 directors
Single member; single director; nominee required; relaxed compliance
New under Companies Act 2013; min Rs.1 lakh authorised capital
Members are primary producers (farmers, artisans); deals in produce
Agricultural producer companies; minimum 10 producer individuals or 2 producer institutions
Company with charitable objects; no profit distribution; operates with licence from Central Govt
Company that holds majority shares (>50%) of another company
Company whose majority shares held by holding company or controlled by holding company
At least 51% shares held by holding or by composition of Board
Company over which another has significant influence (20% or more of voting power) but not subsidiary
Section 2(6) of Companies Act 2013; equity method of accounting
Cultivate habit of saving among members; borrow from and lend to members only
Mutual benefit society; registered as public limited; exempted from many provisions
Charter document; defines scope and objects; company cannot act beyond MoA (ultra vires)
Name clause; Registered Office clause; Objects clause; Liability clause; Capital clause; Association clause
Internal rules and regulations; governs internal management
Allotment of shares; calls on shares; transfer; transmission; voting rights; board meetings; dividends
Invitation to public to subscribe shares/debentures; detailed disclosures required
Risk factors; financials; promoter background; objects of issue; abridged prospectus for retail investors
Issued by ROC (Registrar of Companies) on registration; company becomes legal entity
Conclusive evidence of incorporation; company can commence business
Required for public company to start business; not needed after 2018 amendment (SPICe+)
Abolished for most practical purposes by Companies (Amendment) Act 2019
Private: 2 directors; Public: 3 directors; OPC: 1 director; maximum 15 directors (more by special resolution)
No relationship with company; not related to promoter; professional expertise; listed companies need at least 1/3 independent directors
Listed companies and certain prescribed public companies must have at least one woman director
Minimum 4 meetings per year; gap between two consecutive meetings not more than 120 days
1/3 of total directors or 2 directors, whichever is higher; minimum quorum 2
Duties: act in good faith; not conflict of interest; not achieve undue gain; exercise due diligence
Convicted of offence involving moral turpitude; declared insolvent; unsound mind; debarred by court; company in default in filing returns for 3 years
CEO/MD, CFO, CS (Company Secretary) and whole-time director are KMPs; mandatory for listed and large public companies
Prohibited; company cannot give loans to directors or their relatives except in certain circumstances
Board approval required for transactions with related parties above threshold; shareholder approval for larger transactions

items: Key exam focus: Statutory provisions and thresholds under the Companies Act, 2013.
Important topic: Powers, duties, legal responsibilities, and liabilities of Directors.
Frequent questions: Modes and legal procedures of Winding Up of Companies.

cells: NCLT orders winding up on petition; grounds: special resolution, fraud, just and equitable, failure to file annual returns, regulatory order
Petition to NCLT; Provisional Liquidator; Official Liquidator; distribution of assets
Members or creditors voluntarily wind up without NCLT order
Special resolution; declaration of solvency; winding up by members if solvent, by creditors if insolvent
IBC 2016 now primary insolvency framework; NCLT adjudicates; Liquidation under IBC Chapter III
CIRP first; if fails — Liquidation; Official Liquidator or IP as Liquidator
